title: Time management
examples: How do I know what my priorities really are?
Can you give me an example of breaking down a big project?
What is the best way to use the Pomodoro technique?

explain.say: Today we are learning about managing your time better.
First, we must learn to set our priorities correctly.
For example, studying for a big test is important and not urgent yet.
Next, we will learn how to break big tasks into smaller steps.
For example, writing a big essay becomes much easier in small parts.
The Pomodoro technique uses timed work intervals to keep you focused.

items: Take a long break after four cycles

faq.q: How do I know what my priorities really are?
faq.a: Ask yourself what is most important for your long-term goals. Think about what really matters more than what feels urgent right now. You could also ask yourself, what is the most important thing I must do today?
asks: What should I focus on first?
How do I decide what is most important?

faq.q: Can you give me an example of breaking down a big project?
faq.a: If you have to clean your whole room, you can break it down. First, put away clothes, then clean the desk, and finally vacuum the floor. This makes it less overwhelming. You could also ask, what are the steps for a big task?
asks: How do I start a huge assignment?
What is the best way to tackle a big job?

faq.a: It is a time management method using a timer for focused work. You work intensely for 25 minutes, then take a short break. This helps keep your mind fresh and focused. You could also ask, what is the 25 minute focus method?
asks: How does the Pomodoro technique work?
Is the Pomodoro technique good for studying?

faq.q: Is it better to do everything right away?
faq.a: No, that is usually not effective for time management. It is better to plan and schedule your tasks. Planning helps you see what needs to be done and when. You could also ask, should I do things immediately?
asks: Should I just jump into everything?

faq.q: What if my tasks are too big to break down?
faq.a: If a task feels too big, try breaking it down into the smallest possible action. For example, instead of 'Write report', try 'Find three sources'. Small steps build momentum. You could also ask, what if I get stuck on a task?
asks: How do I start if I feel overwhelmed?
What is the smallest first step I can take?

facts: Prioritizing means deciding what is most important to do first.
Breaking tasks down makes large jobs feel much more manageable.
The Pomodoro technique uses timed intervals of work and rest.
A typical Pomodoro session is 25 minutes of focused work.

quiz.say: If studying for a final exam is important but not due next week, where should it be placed?
quiz.why: This area requires scheduling time so the task does not become a crisis later.

wrong.0: This area is for tasks that do not matter at all.
wrong.1: This area is for things that are urgent but not important.
wrong.3: This area is for things that are both urgent and important.

quiz.say: If you have to write a 1000 word essay, which is the best first step?
quiz.show: Researching sources is the best first step.
quiz.why: Researching provides the necessary information to build the rest of your work.

wrong.1: You cannot write the conclusion without writing the main body first.
wrong.2: You cannot check spelling until the writing process is complete.
wrong.3: While necessary, this is not the core content step.

quiz.say: A student works on a task for 25 minutes, then takes a short break. This method is:
quiz.why: This pattern of focused bursts followed by rest is the definition of the technique.

wrong.0: Deep work implies continuous focus without scheduled breaks.
wrong.1: Task batching means grouping similar small tasks together, not timing work.
wrong.3: Time blocking involves scheduling every minute, not just using timed bursts.
